note: Queries no policy clause answers. The correct retrieve_policy result for each is an empty list. Used by evals/retrieval_baseline.py to measure whether a backend can express 'nothing relevant', and to calibrate the dense similarity floor. Drafted by the assistant; set reviewed to true only after a human has checked every probe against the corpus. Three tiers, easiest first: nonsense, off-domain, and in-product questions outside billing/plan/account policy. The last tier is the one that matters - it is what a real support inbox sends. Probes deliberately avoid the few product features the corpus does mention (API access, SSO, storage, project limits, audit log, export), so none of them has a genuinely relevant clause.
review_notes: Assistant evidence pass, 2026-10-14 (not a human review; reviewed stays false until the label owner signs off). Each probe's top-3 dense and top-2 lexical clauses were read against the query: every hit is a coincidental word match (Monday -> SLA-001.4, change -> PLN-001.5, adding -> SEA-001.4) or a weak semantic neighbour (due-date reminder -> BIL-001.5 renewal notice). None answers its probe. One interpretive point for the reviewer: ESC-001.6 ('where policy is silent ... escalate') applies to every probe, but by the absence of any other matching clause, not by similarity to the query. The empty result is what licenses ESC-001.6, so empty remains the correct retrieval answer; an agent escalating on silence should fetch ESC-001.6 by id. If the reviewer disagrees, these labels change.
